headline: Council welcomes Fukuyama sister city delegation

meeting.summary: The Maui County Council welcomed a Fukuyama City delegation with speeches, music, hula, lei and gifts honoring the sister city relationship.
meeting.recap: The Maui County Council welcomed a delegation from Fukuyama City, Japan, in the Council Chamber.[[0:00:34]] The chair said a Council resolution established the Maui County–Fukuyama City sister city relationship.[[0:00:39]] A sister chamber relationship between Fukuyama and Maui Japanese chambers of commerce existed as of May 31, 1997.[[0:00:57]] The chair said the rose is the official flower of both Fukuyama City and Maui Island.[[0:01:53]] The managing director thanked the Fukuyama visitors on behalf of the mayor.[[0:03:59]] A Council Services Hawaiian language specialist sang the mele (song) Kila Kila o Maui.[[0:13:04]] An assistant clerk danced a hula to Puamana, a mele about a family home in Lahaina.[[0:16:47]] A Fukuyama delegation leader said he hopes to deepen the relationship between Fukuyama and Maui.[[0:23:18]] The president of Fukuyama City University said he hopes for more active ties between younger generations.[[0:27:38]] The chair asked the visitors to come up to receive lei.[[0:29:08]] The visitors gave gifts, including a rose-flavored ramen.[[0:31:28]] A councilmember from Molokaʻi danced a hula to a mele about Molokaʻi.[[0:38:20]] The chair thanked the visitors for coming to commemorate the sister city relationship.[[0:42:56]]

moments.q: Welcome to the Fukuyama City delegation
"It really has the flavor of rose."
